marta: Kicking off bring-up for dewalt-embed-small. Headline: block-int4 (32) introduces a non-linear topk collapse on domain-specific queries (devops/security). Full numbers below.

marta: Summary (en-devops holdout 2k): fp16 recall@5: 0.882; int8: 0.880 (-0.2); int4-block32: 0.816 (-6.6). Precision@1 drop worst in 'security' cohort.

leo: Oof. What quant pipeline and anchors? Any block packing optimizations (bitshuffle) applied?

amarta: Offline quant: quant/pack_block.py --model dewalt/fp16.ckpt --bits 4 --block-size 32 --pack bitshuffle --calib s3://redwood-evals/anchors/dewalt_4k.jsonl --scheme per-block-perchannel. Did not fold residual add.

akshay: Bitshuffle can reorder bytes to improve compression but might amplify block boundary artifacts. Also per-block-perchannel is tricky for small blocks. Can you paste eval command?

marta: Eval used: ```bash
python eval/recall.py --model dewalt-embed-small --weights /models/dewalt/int4_block32.pth --holdout s3://redwood-evals/dewalt/devops_2k.jsonl --k 5 --sim cosine --normalize true --batch 256
```

shay: Have you measured embedding entropy or effective rank pre/post quant? If quant collapses low-variance dims we lose discriminative directions for niche queries.

amarta: Yes, effective rank (participation ratio) fp16: 84.2 -> int4-block32: 62.7. Per-dim var map shows many dims clipped to quant grid near zero.

leo: Two immediate experiments: 1) entropy-preserving clamp: per-dim min-scale to avoid severe compression (clamp scale >= 0.15*median_scale). 2) rank-loss aware calibration: optimize an affine post-transform on anchors minimizing rank/recall tradeoff instead of pure MSE.

akshay: Also try block32 with overlap (stride 16) so blocks share dims; reduces boundary artifacts but increases quant metadata. Could be a good trade.

marta: Queued runs: run_e1 = int4-block32+clamp (anchors 8k stratified), run_e2 = int4-block32-overlap-stride16, run_e3 = int4-block32+affine-rankloss. Configs at s3://redwood-dev/dewalt/onboard/3840004321/*.yaml.

eval-bot: Jobs scheduled: 3840004321-e1,e2,e3. Started 3840004400. ETA ~28m. Will post recall@k, effective-rank plot, and per-cohort k-slope.

shay: Add a targeted devops-subcohort: 'CVE identifiers as queries' and 'short keyphrase' (<=6 tokens). Those are fragile. Also compute top-5 swap-rate vs fp16.

leo: If overlap or clamp recovers >3% on security cohort without >10% perf/size regression we can propose an int4 profile with block-overlap enabled for security-sensitive tenants.

akshay: One more: instrument cheap online fallback: if query embedding l2-norm < threshold or entropy < t -> route to int8. That avoids global fallback.

amarta: Added fallback rule to run_e1 config. Will post results when eval-bot reports back. Thanks :thumbsup:
